routes.label: Separate the pizza cost from the topping cost

question: Doug and Dave shared a pizza with \(8\) equally-sized slices. Doug wanted a plain pizza, but Dave wanted anchovies on half of the pizza. The cost of a plain pizza was \(\$8,\) and there was an additional cost of \(\$2\) for putting anchovies on one half. Dave ate all the slices of anchovy pizza and one plain slice. Doug ate the remainder. Each then paid for what he had eaten. How many more dollars did Dave pay than Doug?
solution:
The plain pizza costs \(\$8\) for eight equal slices, so the plain-pizza cost is \(\$1\) per slice. Half the pizza has anchovies, which means four slices.

Dave eats those four slices and one plain slice, for five slices total. Since he eats all the anchovies, his payment includes the entire \(\$2\) topping charge. He pays \(5+2=7\) dollars.

Doug eats the remaining \(8-5=3\) plain slices and pays \(3\) dollars. Dave therefore pays
\[
7-3=4
\]
more dollars. The answer is \(\boxed{4}\), choice D.
